text:
Memorandum dated April 21, 1972, from the Nevada Department of Administration transmitting comment by the Director, Nevada Department of Fish and Game.
Comment: The State comment expresses fear that providing Federal authority to regulate endangered resident species would weaken the effectiveness of all State wildlife management programs and reduce their enforcement potential.

Response: We would point out that the number of resident endangered species and subspecies now protected by the States only would be relatively few.

The ranges of these populations in each State are quite restricted in most cases. Further, the authority assumed by the Federal Government under the proposed legislation would be returned to the State as soon as effective laws are demonstrated. See reply to Indiana.
<u>Comment</u>: Nevada comments that suspension of hunting and fishing licenses is the responsibility of the State and should remain so.
Response: Reference in HR 4758 to suspension of hunting and fishing
licenses concerns only those licenses over which the Federal Government has
jurisdiction such as waterfowl hunting stamps and Federal permits for hunting
or fishing on Federal lands.
